definition: Oriented FAST and rotated BRIEF (ORB) is a fast robust local feature detector, first presented by Ethan Rublee et al.
details: in 2011, that can be used in computer vision tasks like object recognition or 3D reconstruction. It is based on the FAST keypoint detector and a modified version of the visual descriptor BRIEF (Binary Robust Independent Elementary Features). Its aim is to provide a fast and efficient alternative to SIFT.
story: Picture a child pointing at pictures in a book — cat, car, cloud — learning to see by seeing a thousand examples. It turns a picture into an understanding: this is a cat, that is a stop sign. What your eyes do without thinking, the machine does one careful layer at a time. It is eyes made of arithmetic — pixels become edges, edges become shapes, shapes become meaning. And that is Oriented FAST and rotated BRIEF — giving a machine the gift of sight.
